resources.string: Opal routes the traffic of every app through the Tor network. Websites do not see your IP address, and your provider does not see where you go: to it, this is a connection to a Tor bridge. Bridges help where Tor is blocked.

• It does not carry UDP: calls and games may not work, QUIC falls back to TCP.
• Many services block Tor or show captchas — banks, government services, streaming. You can let them connect directly on the "Apps" tab.
• It is slower than a regular connection.
• It does not make apps anonymous: your accounts still identify you.

To pick bridges for your network, the app asks the Tor Project server (Circumvention Settings API) directly — just like Tor Browser. The request is disguised as a CDN request, but the Tor Project server sees your IP address.
Android will ask whether Opal may create a VPN. Traffic only goes into Tor — the app has no servers of its own.
Connecting is impossible without the permission — you can grant it later

We recommend turning on \"Always-on VPN\" and \"Block connections without VPN\" in system settings: the tunnel then starts by itself after reboots and network changes, and if something breaks, no traffic bypasses Tor.
The notification shows the status and speed and lets you disconnect with one tap.
So that the system does not put the tunnel to sleep, lift background restrictions for Opal. Optional, but on many phones the connection drops otherwise.
On Xiaomi, Huawei, Honor and some others, autostart must be allowed too.
